title: Mini snapshot stitching — personal idea pad
content:
Context / quick brain-dump:

Goal (one-liner): explore a lightweight, relevance-driven micro-snapshot system that stitches short summaries of recent user activity to keep long conversations useful without storing/serving full token histories.

Problem statement:
- Customers are hitting token budget + latency limits when we naive-append entire sessions for long-lived conversations (support agents, coding assistants, docs browsing).
- Full KV caches + long prompts blow up memory or cost on hosted endpoints and dedicated pools.
- Existing eviction heuristics (LRU by token age) lose semantically important context.

Why a "mini-snapshot" approach?
- Create tiny, time-indexed summaries (50-200 tokens) of contiguous interaction windows that capture intent, facts, and anchors.
- Stitch snapshots into a compact context bundle that can be re-expanded or used directly by the model depending on quality/latency needs.

High-level design options (brainstorm):
A) Server-side incremental summarizer (preferred for hosted):
   - After each turn or every N turns, run a low-cost summarization model (small LLM) to produce a micro-snapshot.
   - Store snapshots as indexed objects (time, relevance vectors, pointers to source tokens if needed).
   - At request time: select top-K snapshots by relevance to prompt + include recent full turns up to short window.
   - Optionally expand selected snapshots back into natural-language paragraphs before sending to main model or send as compact items with meta tags.

B) Client-side (edge) sketch:
   - Device/browser builds snapshots and sends them as compact payloads. Good for privacy-sensitive flows.
   - Less control over model selection / cost.

C) Hybrid: cheap server summarizer + on-demand deep rehydrate using longer summarizer/embedding lookups.

Selection & ranking signals:
- Recency weight (decay function)
- Embedding cosine similarity between incoming query and snapshot embedding
- Explicit user flags (pin / important)
- Domain heuristics (e.g., code diffs, system messages higher weight)

Storage model options:
- Flat list of snapshots per session (append-only), small metadata index for fast k-NN via embedding store.
- Tiered retention: hot (last 10 snapshots), warm (30), cold (archive or delete).

User stories (rough):
- As a customer support agent, I want the assistant to remember key customer intent from earlier in the day without re-sending entire logs so that reply latency stays low.
- As a developer using Redwood dedicated, I want snapshots to be reversible (point to original tokens) so I can debug hallucinations.
- As a compliance admin, I want to set retention policy (7/30/90 days) for snapshots independent of full transcripts.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- System produces micro-snapshots that reduce average tokens sent per request by >=30% for long sessions (>2000 tokens) without lowering measured helpfulness by >5% (human-eval).
- Snapshot selection latency adds <=25ms median overhead to routing path for hosted API.
- Admins can configure per-org retention policy in Console.

Metrics to track:
- tokens_sent_per_request (median / p95) before vs after
- mean_reply_time (ms)
- helpfulness_score (human eval / automatic scoring) delta
- snapshot_hit_rate (fraction of convo requests that used at least one snapshot)
- recall_failures (cases where user complains session forgot something pinned in past)

Open implementation questions / risks:
- Summarizer quality vs cost: cheap summarizers might omit critical facts -> need fallback to original turns or explicit verification step.
- Drift: snapshots might become stale; need automatic refresh or TTL.
- Privacy: storing even tiny summaries can be sensitive; must map to org retention/KMS rules.
- Debuggability: when a model uses a snapshot and hallucinates, engineers need a trace back to original tokens. Keep pointers or store provenance hashes.

Experiment plan (3-week spike):
Week 0: narrow scope, pick two verticals (support chat, code assistant).
Week 1: implement server-side summarizer pipeline (simple microservice) + store snapshots as JSON objects, create embeddings index. Quick A/B harness.
Week 2: run live A/B on internal traffic for both verticals, collect token counts, latency, and quick human eval (20 examples / vertical).
Week 3: analyze, triage failure cases, refine snapshot size and ranking heuristics.

Rollout considerations / progressive modes:
- Off by default; opt-in per org via Console feature flag.
- Start with read-only snapshots (no rehydration) then enable re-expansion later.
- Canary on hosted only; Dedicated customers can opt in to running summarizer in their VPC.

UX / API surface ideas:
- New request parameter: session_mode: [full, compact, smart] where smart toggles snapshot stitching.
- Developer endpoint to pin/unpin snapshots and to request provenance for a given response id.
- Console UI: session timeline with micro-snapshots shown, ability to edit or pin snapshots.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Talk to SRE about storage cost estimates (snapshot object size * retention).
- Check with Security on whether snapshot text counts as retained PII (likely yes).
- Prototype summarizer: try 1) instruct-tuned 7B quant, 2) distilled LLM, 3) heuristic template-based summarizer (cheap baseline).
- Wire up an offline eval harness: pairwise comparisons (full-history vs compact-with-snapshots).

Edge cases / small thoughts:
- Multi-user threads: snapshots should include participant role tokens; may need per-party snapshots.
- System messages / tool outputs: prefer to always include these as anchored snapshots.
- For code assistants: snapshots should preserve code snippets as attachments rather than flattened prose to avoid losing grammar.

Unresolved questions to bring to sync w/ Kai & Maya:
- Snapshot canonical format: NL paragraph vs key-value bucket? Which is easier for downstream models to use reliably?
- Optimal snapshot size (start with 100 tokens-ish?)
- How often to re-run summarizer for long idle sessions?

References / quick links:
- INF-2123 (design ticket)
- related: convo-trimmer experiments from last year (check notes from Oct 2024)

Final thought: focus on producing a tiny, debuggable artifact with clear provenance. If we can show token savings + no regression on helpfulness, this is a high-leverage feature for both hosted and dedicated customers.
